question: On 16 July 2023, the Commission and the Tunisian Government signed a memorandum of understanding on a strategic and comprehensive partnership.

The agreement included an important migration component, with the EU committing to provide adequate additional financial support for the necessary acquisitions, training and technical support, in particular for coast guards with a view to improving protection of Tunisia’s borders. In return, Tunisia undertook, for example, to support the return of irregular migrants in Tunisia to their countries of origin.
In October 2023, however, President Kais Saied returned to the Commission the EUR 60 million in EU funds he had already accepted under the agreement. In this context: 1.
Can the Commission give an overview of how the migration component of this memorandum of understanding has been applied to date (EU funds disbursed, actions taken, tangible results achieved, etc.)?
What further steps is the Commission planning to take to strengthen cooperation with Tunisia in the fight against irregular immigration?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.6.2024) On 16 July 2023, the EU and Tunisia signed a memorandum of understanding1 (MoU) for a strategic and global partnership based on five pillars –macroeconomic stability, trade and investment, green energy transition, people-to-people contacts and migration and mobility.

The MoU complements the EU–Tunisia Association Agreement2 and Member States' bilateral initiatives, and prioritises measures against irregular migration, including anti-smuggling operations, border management and returns, with a view to avoiding loss of human lives and developing legal pathways for migration.
The MoU defined a common approach based on upholding human rights and with action to combat criminal networks of migrant smugglers and human traffickers.

Under pillar 5 of the MoU, there has been progress in the implementation of migration-related priorities and programmes totalling EUR 105 million from the 2023 budget under the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument3, as well as on ongoing programmes from the 2022 budget.

Since the beginning of 2024, EUR 53 million from 2023 budget have been contracted, with projects signed in the area of protection and access to basic services (EUR 8 million including EUR 3 million from 2022 budget4), support to voluntary returns from Tunisia to countries of origin and reintegration of Tunisian returnees (EUR 13 million), support to search and rescue (EUR 17 million) and support to the Garde Nationale Maritime (EUR 18 million).

The implementation of the EU-Tunisia MoU has started showing results in the past months. Since September 2023, a slowing down in the pace of arrivals to Italy has been registered, with continued anti-smuggling operations by the Tunisian authorities. In 2024, arrivals to Italy are significantly lower (around one-third) compared to those of the beginning of 2023.

As part of the MoU, the Commission is committed to keep working with the Tunisians on all aspects of migration, including in ensuring protection of migrants and refugees and dignified returns of irregular migrants to countries of origins, in full respect of human rights.
